newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Konsortium eyes port stake, air cargo.
newsitem.headline: Konsortium eyes port stake, air cargo.

text.p: Container haulage and shipping firm Konsortium Perkapalan Bhd said on Tuesday it was interested in acquiring a stake in a port in Malaysia and plans to expand into the air cargo business.
Company group executive chairman Mirzan Mahathir said West Port, on the west coast of the peninsula, would complete Konsortium's plan to build up a logistics network.

"Certainly port management is an area of great interest for us. If there is an opportunity that arises we would be keen to evaluate it," he said when asked by reporters whether he was looking to buy a stake in West Port.

"West Port is important because it has the capacity and can be tailored to customers' needs. It is a greenfield project. It could become a major hub for the region," Mirzan told reporters after a seminar in Kuala Lumpur.
Konsortium has said it was building a goods distribution park in West Port.
Mirzan, eldest son of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, also indicated he was interested in the air cargo business.
"We are not just (interested in) land and sea capabilities but the air cargo business," he said. "The air cargo part is an important part and we are looking to develop that side at some point."
